findings.evidence: notify him by email
findings.rationale: The pronoun 'him' is referentially ambiguous because there are three plausible antecedents in the sentence: the Librarian, the Member, or the Guarantor.

findings.evidence: TBD minutes
findings.rationale: The token expiration duration is left as an unresolved placeholder ('TBD minutes').

findings.evidence: user-friendly; easy to navigate; loads rapidly; standard connections
findings.rationale: Uses subjective, unquantified terms ('user-friendly', 'easy to navigate', 'loads rapidly', 'standard connections') without measurable thresholds or test criteria.

findings.evidence: TBD consecutive times
findings.rationale: The maximum renewal count is left as an unresolved placeholder ('TBD consecutive times').

findings.evidence: validate item eligibility within 2 seconds and issue the loan receipt
findings.rationale: Describes only the happy path for barcode eligibility validation without specifying the system response or error handling when an item is ineligible or the barcode scan fails.

findings.evidence: the allowed maximum number of active hold requests
findings.rationale: References a numeric hold limit ('the allowed maximum number of active hold requests') without specifying the actual numeric value.

findings.evidence: borrow up to 8 physical items simultaneously
findings.rationale: Specifies a simultaneous borrowing limit of 8 physical items, contradicting SD-009 which caps active Members in good standing at 5 physical items.

findings.evidence: standard loan period for circulating print books to 21 calendar days
findings.rationale: Sets the standard loan duration for circulating print books to 21 calendar days, contradicting SD-010 which sets it to 14 calendar days.

findings.evidence: self-register online with only an email address and immediately check out physical books without Librarian ID verification
findings.rationale: Allows unverified online self-registration with only an email address and immediate checkout without Librarian ID verification, contradicting SD-001 which requires a Librarian to verify government-issued photo ID and record full name, email, and phone number before account creation.

findings.evidence: remain held indefinitely until the requesting Member explicitly cancels the hold
findings.rationale: Requires reserved items on the pickup shelf to be held indefinitely until explicit cancellation, contradicting SD-011 which expires holds after 72 hours and notifies the next Member in queue.

findings.evidence: send an overdue email and/or suspend borrowing privileges and/or apply a penalty flag
findings.rationale: Stacked 'and/or' connectives leave it ambiguous which combination of actions is mandatory when an item becomes 7 days overdue.

findings.evidence: shall be reviewed, approved, and recorded with a reason code
findings.rationale: Uses passive voice without identifying which human role or system component is responsible for reviewing, approving, and recording fine waiver requests.

findings.evidence: if appropriate
findings.rationale: Uses the non-binding qualifier 'if appropriate', making SMS alert dispatch discretionary and untestable.

findings.evidence: before the due date if appropriate
findings.rationale: Omits the exact lead time before the due date and the concrete eligibility conditions governing when SMS due-date alerts must be dispatched.

findings.evidence: TBD years
findings.rationale: The archival retention period for payment receipts is left as an unresolved placeholder ('TBD years').

findings.evidence: overdue fine of $1.25 USD per overdue day per item with no maximum cap
findings.rationale: Sets the overdue fine rate to $1.25 USD per day with no cap, contradicting SD-019 which sets it to $0.50 USD per day capped at $20.00 USD per item.

findings.evidence: permitted to renew borrowed items online at any time regardless of any unpaid overdue fine balance
findings.rationale: Allows item renewals regardless of unpaid overdue fine balances, contradicting SD-020 which blocks any Member with an unpaid fine balance exceeding $5.00 USD from borrowing or renewing items.

findings.evidence: Patron's; Patron profile screen
findings.rationale: Introduces the term 'Patron' instead of the established term 'Member' used throughout earlier requirements (starting in SD-001 and SD-009).

findings.evidence: quickly; many users
findings.rationale: Uses unquantified terms 'quickly' (no response-time threshold) and 'many users' (no concurrency target).

findings.evidence: where possible
findings.rationale: Uses the non-binding qualifier 'where possible', leaving it undefined when query term highlighting is required versus optional.

findings.evidence: sufficient ISBN matching accuracy; acceptable response times
findings.rationale: Uses subjective, unquantified qualifiers ('sufficient', 'acceptable') without measurable accuracy or latency criteria.

findings.evidence: efficiently; large batch MARC21 files; noticeable system slowdown
findings.rationale: Uses vague, unmeasured criteria ('efficiently', 'large', 'noticeable system slowdown') with no throughput, file-size, or performance bounds.

findings.evidence: shall detect the active references
findings.rationale: Specifies detecting active loans or holds on a bibliographic record deletion attempt, but omits the resulting system behavior (such as blocking deletion or returning an error).

findings.evidence: TBD intervals
findings.rationale: The full database backup schedule is left as an unresolved placeholder ('TBD intervals').

findings.evidence: important administrative actions; timely manner; appropriate period
findings.rationale: Uses subjective, unquantified terms ('important', 'timely manner', 'appropriate period') without defining which actions, latency bounds, or retention duration apply.

findings.evidence: If the primary database node becomes unreachable for more than 10 seconds, the Failover Manager shall log event FAILOVER-01.
findings.rationale: Specifies the 10-second unreachability fault trigger for the Failover Manager but only requires logging event FAILOVER-01, omitting the actual failover, recovery, or alerting action.

findings.evidence: adequate transport security; clear error messages
findings.rationale: Uses subjective, unquantified terms ('adequate', 'clear') without specifying security standards/protocols or concrete error message criteria.

findings.evidence: accept any Member password of at least 8 characters
findings.rationale: Accepts any password of at least 8 characters, contradicting SD-002 which requires at least 12 characters containing uppercase, lowercase, and numeric characters.

findings.evidence: keep authenticated web portal sessions active for 60 minutes of user inactivity
findings.rationale: Sets the web portal inactivity session timeout to 60 minutes, contradicting SD-004 which terminates sessions after 15 minutes of inactivity.

findings.evidence: encrypt all Member passwords using reversible AES-256 encryption so Administrators can decrypt and retrieve forgotten passwords
findings.rationale: Requires reversible AES-256 encryption of passwords so Administrators can decrypt and retrieve them, contradicting SD-003 which mandates one-way bcrypt hashing (cost factor 12) and forbids storing or retrieving plaintext passwords.
